evidence_summary: CRISPR screen identified AP-3 as essential for oncogenic Gα endolysosomal recruitment; disruption of AP-3 binding motif in Gα suppressed cell proliferation and in vivo tumor growth and metastasis; tethering Gα to endolysosomes rescued signaling.

validated_targets.experimental_detail: Disruption of the AP-3 binding motif in Gα (GNAQ) caused mislocalization and potently suppressed tumor growth and metastasis in vivo, while tethering to endolysosomes rescued oncogenic signaling.
Disruption of the AP-3 binding motif in Gα (GNA11) caused mislocalization and potently suppressed tumor growth and metastasis in vivo, while tethering to endolysosomes rescued oncogenic signaling.

Genome-wide CRISPR screen identified AP-3 adaptor protein complex as essential mediator of Gα endolysosomal trafficking; loss of AP-3 impaired Gα-driven signaling and proliferation in uveal melanoma cells.

title: Oncogenic Gα signaling requires AP-3-dependent recruitment to the endolysosomal compartment.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
